LIV Golf: Graeme McDowell becomes latest player to confirm exit from breakaway tour
Graeme McDowell is the latest player to announce he is leaving LIV Golf; the breakaway league is looking to relaunch for the 2027 season with new investment; the Northern Irishman follows in the footsteps of Jon Rahm, Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton, who will not participate in LIV 2.0
Monday 26 October 2026 17:49, UK
Graeme McDowell has confirmed he will follow the lead of Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and Ian Poulter, among others, by becoming the latest player to leave LIV Golf.
The 2010 US Open Champion revealed the news in a social media post on Monday, but the 47-year-old did not elaborate on his future plans.
"I've decided not to pursue LIV 2.0," the Northern Irishman wrote on X.
"I'm grateful for the opportunity I've had over the last four years and want to thank everyone who has been part of that journey.
"I look forward to the next chapter of my career."
LIV Golf is currently plotting out its future after its former backers, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), announced in April that it would be ending its financing of the breakaway league at the end of the 2026 season.
The league was left searching for new investment, but secured financing from BC Partners Credit before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and citing its intentions to relaunch again in 2027 in a new league, dubbed LIV 2.0.
The move left some LIV players contemplating their futures on the tour, with two-time major winner Rahm reaching a separation agreement in October to leave due to 'unacceptable terms' proposed for LIV 2.0.
His compatriot, Sergio Garcia, has also ended his contract, while Hatton announced on social media on Friday that he too would "not be a part of LIV 2.0".
BC Partners had set a deadline of October 25 for players to commit to the league going forward, with a handful of players having announced they would re-sign.
McDowell, who was a part of LIV Golf's OKGC side, joined the breakaway league in 2022.
His last start at a DP World Tour event, outside of the majors, came at the 2022 BMW PGA Championship.
digest_he:
השחקן גרים מקדואל אישר כי הוא עוזב את סבב LIV Golf ולא ייקח חלק בעונת 2027 של הליגה, המכונה LIV 2.0. הודעתו של השחקן בן ה-47 פורסמה ברשת החברתית, בה ציין כי הוא אסיר תודה על התקופה ומצפה לפרק הבא בקריירה שלו.

הליגה מתכננת את עתידה לאחר שקרן ההשקעות הציבורית של ערב הסעודית הפסיקה את המימון שלה בסוף שונת 2026. לאחר מכן הבטיחה הליגה מימון חדש מחברת BC Partners Credit, הגישה בקשה להגנה מפני פשיטת רגל לפי פרק 11 והודיעה על כוונתה להקים מחדש את הליגה.

השינויים הובילו לכך ששחקנים בולטים נוספים, כמו ג'ון רהם וטיפיר האטון, הודיעו גם הם על עזיבתם לאחר שלא הגיעו להסכמות על תנאי ההמשך. מקדואל, שזכה באליפות ארצות הברית הפתוחה ב-2010, הצטרף לסבב הפרישה בשנת 2022.
